page.description: ImmortalWrt 25.12.2 for x86/64: compare image types, download firmware images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: An OpenWrt variant maintained for mainland-China users, published as per-target firmware trees with the same image names and layout as OpenWrt.
pros: Per-target SHA-256 sums are published next to the images.
Same x86/64 image set as OpenWrt: combined EFI and BIOS layouts with squashfs or ext4 rootfs.
Release numbering and target directories follow OpenWrt, so its documentation mostly applies.
An old stable (24.10.6) still gets limited security and bug fixes.
cons: The download index does not document writing these images to USB, so ROMinit lists them as download-only.
A fork with China-focused defaults and packages; it is not the upstream OpenWrt project.
Development snapshots are unattended daily builds the publisher calls generally not tested.
No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for ImmortalWrt; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: These are raw disk images for the x86/64 target. The project publishes the images and their SHA-256 sums but no install guide; writing a combined image overwrites the partition table of the target device. The combined-efi variants boot UEFI, the plain ones legacy BIOS.

editions.name: x86/64 SquashFS Combined EFI
editions.description: SquashFS rootfs with the combined partition layout booting UEFI (and BIOS via hybrid MBR); the default x86/64 image.
editions.usbNote: 18 MB gzipped raw disk image for the target drive. Writing a combined image overrides its partition table.

editions.name: x86/64 ext4 Combined EFI
editions.description: ext4 rootfs with the combined partition layout booting UEFI; more usable space than squashfs, no failsafe mode.
editions.usbNote: 21 MB gzipped raw disk image for the target drive. Writing a combined image overrides its partition table.

editions.name: x86/64 SquashFS Combined
editions.description: SquashFS rootfs with the combined partition layout for legacy BIOS boot.
editions.usbNote: 18 MB gzipped raw disk image for the target drive. Writing a combined image overrides its partition table.

editions.name: x86/64 ext4 Combined
editions.description: ext4 rootfs with the combined partition layout for legacy BIOS boot.
editions.usbNote: 21 MB gzipped raw disk image for the target drive. Writing a combined image overrides its partition table.
